 The biggest thing Bill Self can learn about his team during Players Era Eight
 The KU head coach discussed the event and what he wants to learn about his team.
 Michael Swain 0 Bill Self thinks he will learn plenty about his team during the Players Era Eight, which begins on Tuesday.  His squad is set to play three games in three days, and the action begins on Tuesday night at 8:30 p.m. CT as KU faces off against a 3-0  UNLV  team that is coming off a win over  Stanford  late last week.  The Jayhawks will play either Auburn or West Virginia in the second round and could play Houston or Florida on Thursday depending on how the matchups fall.
 Self has been clear that he likes the potential depth KU has. Now, with Melvin Council Jr. out, it impacts KU's depth in the backcourt, but the Jayhawks are still strong on the wing and in the front court. Self is eager to see how his depth is tested.
 "I think we'll learn a lot about our team," Self said. "We'll also probably learn a lot about our depth because in three games in three days, obviously deeper teams would have an advantage, and can we actually take advantage of people that way? I thought the bench was unbelievable the first half the other night. I thought they were about as good as our starters."
 Although KU only got 12 bench points in the Champions Classic, Self noted the bench players made an impact beyond scoring. Trent Perry made effort plays and got KU two extra possessions and assisted two baskets. Christian Reeves scored eight points and grabbed four rebounds during his 12 minutes of action. Keanu Dawes and Dennis Parker Jr. combined for seven rebounds and three assists during their minutes.
 As it pertains to KU's depth, Self wants to see some players step up and push into a different tier on the roster.
 "I think I'd like to learn more about, how we can get to seven type starters as opposed to five? And if we're able to do that, that'll allow our bench to have more continuity," Self said.
 He likely won't come off the bench during the Players Era Eight, but Leroy Blyden Jr. could be a candidate to make a statement. The Toledo transfer came off the bench in KU's first two games of the season but he's now tasked with starting alongside Taylen Kinney .
 Against Kentucky , the duo combined for 12 points on 3 for 19 shooting from the field. But, they combined for nine assists, four turnovers, three steals and four rebounds. Self isn't hung up on the shooting, though.
 "I thought they both played really well," Self said. "They didn't hold us back at all. They actually were as important as anybody to us winning the game because they controlled it. We didn't turn it over, and they controlled the pace for the most part and guarded extremely well. Even though numbers don't say it, that game was kind of in their hands. If you have to shoot the ball well to play well, then you're probably more of a shooter in a lot of ways than you are a player." 
 The Jayhawks go into the Players Era Eight with some wind in their sails following the win over Kentucky. Self wants to see how the handle success and if they can continue doing the things they did well in the Champions Classic.
 "If we start feeling ourselves too much, obviously that's not a formula for success," Self said. "You want to play hungry. I thought we played hungry the other day. But I also thought we played with passion and joy. A lot of smiles out there. A lot of good personality. You're obviously going to play better when you play happy. There's a competitive edge to it that obviously is so important. But you got to be able to have fun too and those guys were having fun."
